collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 5-12)

collection.description: A child asks why an elder always keeps a packed bundle by the door: tell them why, or say it is just a habit.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) always keeps a bundle by the door of (subject.his/her) hut: a rolled mat, a water gourd, a knife, dried fish, a cord. It's always packed. It has been packed (friend)'s whole life. Today (friend) asks why (subject) keeps a bundle ready if (subject.he/she) never goes anywhere.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) is quiet for a moment. "The people who raised me always kept one," (subject.he/she) says. "Their people had to leave a place in a hurry once, long ago, with nothing. So they always kept one ready, just in case. I've never needed it. I just feel better with it there." (friend) looks at the bundle. "Can I have one too?" (subject) thinks. "You don't need one. But if you want one, I'll help you make it." (friend) makes one. It's mostly snacks.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Old habit," says (subject). "Don't worry about it." (friend) doesn't. But later, watching (subject) check the bundle, retie the cord and set it back exactly where it was, (friend.he/she) sees something on (subject)'s face that isn't just habit. (friend) doesn't ask again. (friend.He/she) just moves (friend.his/her) toys so they're not in the way of the bundle.
